answer.evidence: The entire structure is drawn in pure front elevation. The horizontal support beams (rows 11-12 and 19-20) are flat 2px bars with no visible top surface. answer.main_body: wooden ema rack with tiled roof and stone base
answer.evidence: The entire frame, hanging rails, and bottom stone base are drawn in flat front elevation with no visible top surfaces (the rails are 1-2px flat lines and the base shows only a south face with a 1px highlight). The roof is also drawn flatly without ridge depth.

answer.main_body: ema rack frame with hanging plaques
answer.evidence: The rack frame consists of 1px horizontal beams (rows 12 and 20) with no visible top faces, completely flat vertical plaques, and a base plinth drawn in front elevation without a visible top surface. The frame structure is drawn as a pure front elevation.
The small roof covering the rack shows 8 rows of tiled downward slope viewed from above (rows 1-8). The stone base at the bottom also shows a distinct top surface (rows 28-29) above its front face.
